evidence.codeCommit: #1149 — loadCustomerContext refuses an ambiguous phone match · 2026-08-09 — the opt-out vocabulary collapsed to ONE shared list (shared/smsOptOutKeywords.ts). It had drifted into three copies: the index query that decides suppression matched 10 words, while the inbound handler that reacts live and the instrumentation that attributes opt-outs each matched 5. Nobody went un-suppressed (the index re-derives from raw inbound bodies and is the real net), but STOPALL / REVOKE / OPT OUT produced no confirmation reply, no sms.opt_out compliance row, and stayed sendable until the 5-minute cache turned over 2026-09-23 OPT-OUT OVER-MATCH: the live unsubscribe rule in server/services/smsResponseParser.ts matched any reply that STARTS with a keyword, so a visit ('Stop by around 3?', 'stop over after work', 'End of the day works') silently unsubscribed the customer from every text. Only stop by/in/over/at/off and end of/up are now carved out and go to a person (they cannot be a revocation); every other reply opening with a keyword, punctuated or phrased ('Stop.', 'stop texting me'), still unsubscribes, since missing a real opt-out is the worse error. 2026-09-23 REVOCATION FIRST (audit item B): PATTERNS is first-hit and the opt-out rules sat after confirm/cancel/decline, so 'STOP. Cancel all texts' CANCELLED the booking and recorded no opt-out, and 'Stop texting me, too expensive' became a declined estimate. Revocation now runs first; a phrase rule catches explicit plain-English revocations ('cancel all texts', 'stop texting me', 'don't text me' incl. iOS curly apostrophes, 'no more texts', 'take me off your list', 'unsubscribe me'); the visit carve-outs are same-line only and narrowed, so 'Stop at once', 'stop off my list', 'End of discussion' and 'STOP' + a new line unsubscribe. A bare 'Cancel' stays cancel-appointment (consent-ledger design note F5 leaves it to counsel). 2026-09-24 P1 REVIEW HARDENING: negated revocations (for example 'Don't stop texting me', 'Never stop texting me', 'I do not want to unsubscribe') now route to a person with no autoAction, and remove/take language only opts out when it names an SMS/list object, so booking-scoped requests such as 'remove me from tomorrow's appointment' cannot become durable global SMS opt-outs. 2026-09-29 AUDIT F3: (1) a spoken do-not-call survives an SMS opt-in. YES opts in only an SMS-suppressed number, never a voice-only one; markPhoneOptedIn keeps opted_out=1 + VOICE for a do-not-call row and updates the caches from the row read back; a text STOP on a do-not-call row becomes SMS+VOICE (a full opt-out) so a later START falls back to VOICE, never to callable; START/UNSTOP/YES grant sms_* ledger scopes only (design rule 4), not 'all'. Before this, YES or STOP-then-START wrote opted_out=0 over a VOICE row, and the voice recovery/follow-up lanes could call a number that had said 'stop calling'. (2) Parser: 'stop at'/'stop off'/'end of' are allow-listed (once / my list / discussion...), so 'Stop at five ok?' and 'End of September is better' go to a person; 'Why did you stop texting me?', 'I'll stop texting you' and 'cancel text me when you have an opening' no longer unsubscribe (the last also no longer auto-cancels); the negated span is removed instead of the whole message, so 'You guys never stop texting me. STOP' unsubscribes.

Before this, three voice crons each ran their OWN narrower query (customers.smsOptOut only -- ignoring sms_preferences, the inbound STOP log and carrier blocks) inside catch { /* fail-soft */ }, so an unreachable DB produced an EMPTY opt-out set and the whole batch was called; confirmationCalls.ts had no consent check at all. stale:true is NOT 'five minutes old' (that is the TTL, i.e. the FRESH path) -- it is returned only when a refresh FAILED and the cache age is UNBOUNDED, so every lane treats it as unreadable. Automated lanes THROW so cron_log records a failed run; the operator lane (routers/vapi.ts makeFollowUpCall) REFUSES with a reason, because a silent no-op reads as a broken button. Operator decision 2026-09-16: FCFS shop holds no slots, so a confirmation call is outreach and is gated -- the business fact makes that answer, not the cron's name. PR #2718 candidate (876f6352b): retention email recipients are now syntax-validated before the batch is sliced and before transport; validation trims only harmless outer whitespace, lowercases only the domain, and refuses ambiguous repairs. Malformed CRM rows are skipped with customerId + EMAIL_CAMPAIGNS_INVALID_EMAIL only, so invalid values cannot be sent to Resend or occupy the 15-recipient batch forever. 2026-09-29 AUDIT F4b: a do-not-call said on an INBOUND call now reaches this index. routes/webhooks/vapi.ts persistTranscriptDoNotCallBeforeAck returned early unless call.type was outboundPhoneCall, so a customer who rang the shop (or called back after an automated call) and said 'stop calling me' was never written to sms_preferences, and the recovery/follow-up/confirmation lanes that read loadSuppressionIndex() could call them (47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10): revocation by any reasonable method). The check now runs for every direction, still before the webhook 200 (503 only when the write fails, not when there is no usable caller ID), and takes the broadest request across the call. The inbound receptionist gets recordDoNotCall (same handler, no hang-up; the result says endCall:false). capabilities.name: Once-per-shop-day cron cadence (boot-phase-proof)

evidence.codeCommit: ROS-081 — four businessHoursOnly jobs moved out of the 24h daily tier into the 2h hourly tier, plus a new per-JOB `oncePerShopDay` claim (claimOncePerShopDay) in server/cron/scheduler.ts
tests: server/__tests__/cron-cadence.test.ts (26), mutation-verified. The daily tier is a 24h setInterval whose PHASE is set by process start, so a pod booted at 03:00 ET fired it at 03:00 ET every day — outside 07:00-20:59, so runTier() skipped every businessHoursOnly job in it indefinitely. 10 of 24 possible boot hours starve it. Worse, that pass still called resetSkipCount('daily') BEFORE the job loop, so it also told the boot guard 'daily already ran today' and suppressed the next startup fire — a tier reporting a completed run having produced nothing (ROS-078 class). Prod cron_log 2026-07-29: opportunity-queue-refresh ran 1 times in 7 days, expected about 7. Affected: referral-loop-closer and vip-auto-recognition (BOTH send customer SMS), opportunity-queue-refresh (Decision Inbox feed), promise-sweep (Promise Ledger escalation). The fix has two halves and BOTH are load-bearing: relocation gives every job a firing inside business hours from all 24 boot hours, and the per-JOB claim makes 'the tier fired' no longer readable as 'the job ran'. Tests pin the ET calendar boundary including the DST shift (a hardcoded -05:00 would be an hour wrong all summer), the starvation simulation across all 24 boot hours, the tier-placement invariant scoped to the daily block, and the ordering that keeps the claim INSIDE acquireCronLock — two pods that each read 'not yet run today' would both claim and both send, the v1.7 duplicate-SMS class. Three mutations verified to turn the suite RED: job back in the daily tier (1 fail), claim moved before the lock (2 fails), hardcoded -05:00 offset (5 fails).

Derived defect pinned in the same change: selfHealing judged these jobs on the raw 120min tier interval (120x3 + 15h overnight grace = 21h allowance against a normal ~24h gap), which would have fired a false CRON STALE every day AND auto-reset the job's running flag. It now uses an explicit two-shop-day allowance and reports the cadence the job actually keeps.

Note the observation is phase-sensitive: prod booted 09:09 ET on 2026-08-03, inside business hours, which is exactly why the defect looked healthy on a same-day spot check. PROMOTION PATH: exposure is held at `internal` ONLY because the ledger forbids claiming `production` before live_verified — the four crons it governs already run autonomously in prod. Promote to live_verified + production together, with evidence.liveRuns carrying the cron_log read; do not promote on the strength of the test suite.

capabilities.name: The attribution queue says what its confidence numbers mean, and that they are not probabilities

evidence.codeCommit: 2026-09-18. The review queue showed 0.9 and 0.75 beside real invoices, and an operator confirming money reads those as percentages. Reading the producer, they are ordinal labels for two evidence recipes that differ by EXACTLY ONE FACT - whether the service text overlapped - and neither has ever been calibrated against outcomes. lib/attributionConfidenceBands.ts names each band, states the evidence that produced it, and states what would RAISE it, which is the only actionable part. bandMix reports inferredPct, the share of rows resting on inference rather than a recorded link. The card renders the mix and, above 80% inferred, says plainly that confirming in bulk is guessing in bulk - which is how the eight-calls-one-invoice over-count happened.
evidence.tests: 20 tests in server/__tests__/attributionConfidenceBands.test.ts. The producer's real ladder is mapped case by case; only VERIFIED is observed and every other band is marked inference. An empty queue reports inferredPct null, not 0 - unmeasured is not measured-zero. The calibration caveat is PINNED BY ASSERTION, including the sentence admitting nobody has measured the hit rate, so if that ever becomes false the caveat has to change with it. Positive control asserts the mix discriminates rather than returning a constant. 169 test files, 2,135 passed, exit 0.
evidence.liveRuns: NONE. The bands have not been observed against a production queue.

blockers.description: THE BANDS ARE UNCALIBRATED AND SAY SO. Nobody has measured how often a phone-and-time match turns out to be the right invoice, so the ordering is evidence-strength, not probability. Calibrating it needs a labelled sample of confirmed and rejected decisions, which does not exist because the decision log is young. Inventing a percentage would have been the defect this module exists to prevent.

The 80% inferred threshold that triggers the bulk-confirm warning is a judgement, not a measurement. It is coarse on purpose - the module's job is to make an inference-heavy queue obvious, not to score it.

blockers.description: CLOSED IN REVIEW 2026-09-22, recorded so it is not re-opened as unexamined. dueAt was nextOpenAt(), which returns NOW when the shop is already OPEN - so a callback promised at 10am Tuesday was due at 10am Tuesday and overdue one second later, and the sweep would escalate it then stamp it missed after 48h. Not a closed-hours-only path: escalate is exposed to the OUTBOUND follow-up assistant, whose script says we will have someone call you back today, and those calls are placed during business hours by design. Now nextCloseAt(): the close of the business day the shop can next act on. DERIVED not invented - the outbound script states today so close-of-business is the shop own stated bound, and the inbound script states no time but the shop can only act while open, so closing time is the last moment it can honour the promise that day. Refusing during open hours was rejected as worse: most calls arrive while open, so voice promises would have existed only for after-hours calls. 13 tests in shared/nextCloseAt.test.ts, including one that pins the defect itself (nextOpenAt returns now during open hours) and a positive control that every result is STRICTLY after now.

RESOLVED 2026-09-22, downgraded from P2 rather than deleted so the history stays readable. Migration 0125 (uq_promise_source, renamed from a colliding 0103) is APPLIED and VERIFIED in production TiDB: Non_unique 0 on (source_kind, source_id, promise_type). The read-then-write race is now closed by the database rather than by hopeful ordering. APPLYING IT MOVED A FAILURE MODE INSTEAD OF DELETING ONE. createPromise rethrows anything that is not a missing-table error, so the same concurrency the index was added for would now throw ER_DUP_ENTRY into the VAPI webhook path. createVoicePromise interprets that one signal as {created:false, reason:duplicate} - which is what it is - re-reading through the same findExisting() helper the pre-check uses, and RETHROWS when no row is found, because a duplicate-key error with no matching row is a different constraint. MySQL and TiDB UNIQUE indexes permit unlimited NULLs, so the index cannot reject any write the currently-deployed code can make. The table also held 0 rows at apply time.

Only the two SCRIPTED offer paths create promises. A commitment Nick improvises outside escalate/scheduleCallback is still unrecorded. Detecting that from speech was deliberately not attempted: voiceClaimGuard is a PROHIBITION detector (unbacked_callback_promise), not a commitment detector, and its regex does not even match the prompt's own scripted callback line - verified by executing the regex against that exact sentence.

Voice promises still cannot be KEPT automatically - the callback happens on the counter phone, which this system cannot observe. Mitigated rather than solved: voice promises are now EXCLUDED from the kept-rate (promiseLedgerStats) and reported by voicePromiseBacklog as a to-do list with no rate at all, so an unmeasurable numerator can no longer defame the shop in the morning brief. The obligations are still real and the OVERDUE count surfaces them; what is absent is proof of closure, and it is labelled as absent rather than scored as failure.

blockers.description: The inline schema-guard DDL in routers/nick/intelligence.ts and drizzle/0126 must stay identical by hand; nothing checks that they agree. Same standing rule 0094 states for the table itself.

cancelled is the only inert terminal status the expected_arrivals enum offers without DDL, so a same-visit sibling wears that word with a superseded-by note rather than a superseded status. The no-show sweep still fires on any expected row older than two days regardless of whether a sibling row for the same customer reconciled OUTSIDE the 3-day window. Any rate built on status = no_show is a lead-conversion rate wearing a no-show costume. A provenance column (customer_stated vs assistant_directed), or a prompt change that reserves bookSlot for an explicit commitment, would make the number mean what it says; neither is attempted here.

bookSlot now files a short spoken number under the VAPI caller ID, logs why recordExpectedArrival refused a row, and returns not_recorded so the assistant re-asks for the number (2026-10-03: one 12:33Z call left no row and no log). blockers.description: The holdout permutation gate has decided a live run (2026-10-10 02:20Z: +4/-0/=5 of 9, p=0.063, refuted); the success-cohort veto and the sealed confirmation have not, because no candidate has passed holdout yet. With 13 holdout seeds and 3 repeats a candidate needs about 5 improved discordant calls and 0 worsened to clear alpha 0.05 (4/0 reads p=0.0625); ties (5 of 9 here) buy nothing. If near misses repeat, the lever is more holdout seeds or repeats inside the 45-minute budget, not a looser alpha.

The replay is a proxy lane: GHOST_AGENT_MODEL (default deepseek-v4-pro), temperature 0, 700 tokens, no tools, while the code pushes gpt-4o at 0.4, 250 tokens, with tools (vapi.ts buildAssistantConfig). Moving the replay onto the live lane is an operator cost decision. Until then every verdict is a proxy-lane verdict, and the lane record names the requested replay model only (ghostReplay discards the model that served, so an AI_FORCE_* reroute is invisible).

Calibration is simulated: the A/A and power figures come from seeded simulations, not real traces, and the resolution judge has no labelled calibration set. Each sealed confirmation holds alpha 0.05 for the candidate it confirms; the share of false confirmations across many weeks is not bounded (it would need a persisted confirmation count).

capabilities.name: Content experiment winners must survive a permutation test

evidence.codeCommit: branch claude/peaceful-pascal-988w9o: shared/contentExperiments.ts evaluateExperiment decides only at the planned looks DECISION_LOOKS = 12 / 24 / 48 / 96 reported posts per arm (then every 48), splits WINNER_ALPHA 0.05 across them (0.0125 per look; Bonferroni, stateless, no bookkeeping of looks taken), requires a >= 10% lead AND a two-sided permutation p <= 0.0125 between the top two arms (x runners-up with more than two arms), calls a tie (< 10% lead; 'retire this variable') only from the 48-per-arm look, and between looks or short of significance returns insufficient_data naming the next look — the experiment keeps running. For WEIGHTED_AVERAGE metrics (avg_watch_time, ig_reels_avg_watch_time, avgWatchTimeMs) the permutation statistic is the reach-weighted mean gap, the same quantity armRates ranks on (before: plain per-post values, so the ranking and its p-value were computed on different quantities). permutationP is exact up to 50,000 relabellings, fixed-seed Monte Carlo (20,000) beyond. Pre-merge audit 2026-10-08: the single-look rule was being re-applied every day by the resolver (optional stopping) and 'under 10% -> tie' concluded before any test.
tests: shared/contentExperimentsValidity.test.ts (16): CONTROL — the replaced rule crowns a winner between identical arms in > 60% of first looks (measured 85.8% at 4 posts/arm); walked daily the way the resolver runs (4 … 100 posts per arm, the first verdict scored): identical arms end as a false winner in <= 6% of experiments (measured 3.8%; 69.5% tie, 26.8% still running at 100), a doubled share rate is found >= 95% (measured 99.8%, mean first verdict 27.5 posts/arm) and a 1.5x rate >= 70% (measured 85.0%), never on the wrong arm; decision-look arithmetic; between looks -> insufficient_data naming the next look whatever the lead; a noise-explainable lead at 12 -> insufficient_data; arms within 10% at 12 -> 'too close to call yet', at 48 -> tie; a decisive lead at a look -> winner; permutationP exact case, p = 1 on identical samples, Monte Carlo determinism, equal weights == unweighted, the weighted exact path matches an independent brute-force enumeration of weighted-mean gaps; a reach-weighted lead on avg_watch_time is a winner where the old per-post test (kept as CONTROL) could not tell the arms apart. Mutations: removing the decision-look guard turns the A/A walk red; dropping the weights turns the weighted-metric test red.

shared/contentExperiments.test.ts, server/services/contentExperimentStore.test.ts, server/cron/jobs/contentExperimentResolve.test.ts and shared/contentExperimentPresets.test.ts (11) green on the sequential rule.

blockers.description: No experiment has resolved under the new rule in production. A verdict is now possible only at 12 / 24 / 48 / 96 reported posts per arm; every other day the resolver notes 'between decision looks' with the next look — that is the rule working, not the lane failing.

capabilities.name: A car parked through a sign-edge restart keeps its visit: restored visits are held from departing for a bounded window and a still car in the same spot continues its visit under the old object id, with no departure and no new arrival; ambiguity refuses and the visit departs as before

evidence.codeCommit: Follow-up to camera N-series PR C (branch claude/dreamy-newton-0iob20, 2026-10-08), camera audit 2026-10-07 section 5. camera-bridge edge_main.reconcile_restart force-ends the restored sightings (dwell frozen at the last activity), holds their visits in DEPARTING (visitd VisitTracker.hold_departures, transient, never persisted) and arms vision VisionPipeline.arm_restart_rebind. A track that is confirmable with 3+ hits, never moved, sits in a zone the restored sighting was still in, has IoU >= 0.5 with its last box and was born <= 120 s after that car was last seen reports under the old object id, so visitd resurrects the sighting: no departure row, no new arrival, arrivedAt and the stored episode id kept (the upsert keeps a stored value over a null). One track over two restored cars, two tracks over one, a moved car or a longer gap refuses. The window opens on the first decoded frame and closes after 20 s or once every entry is decided. Flags --restart-rebind-seconds (0 disables) and --restart-rebind-max-gap-seconds; counters edge_restart_continuations_total and edge_restart_departures_total. Merged in #2934 as main d679d066; NicksMax pulled it 2026-10-08 22:50:37Z and the supervisor's code-change rule restarted the sign edge onto it at 22:51:04Z. 2026-10-09 (branch claude/dreamy-newton-0iob20): the episode-id seam is closed. visitd's ledger stores each visit's stitcher episode id (visits.episode_id, an additive nullable column with an idempotent ALTER; latest non-null wins, a NULL is never written), reconcile_restart restores it onto the continuing track, so a continued car whose track later dies and is re-acquired keeps its episode and counts once on the Lot. Visits already open when the deploy restarts the edge have no stored episode and fall back to the old behaviour once. Review of that change found the stamping it relies on was wrong for two cars: VisionPipeline._emit stamped the calling track's episode onto every emission visitd returned, including another visit's timer-driven CONFIRMED_ARRIVAL, so two overlapping arrivals counted as one on the Lot (pre-existing) and the new ledger column would have kept the wrong episode across restarts.
